title: Software control-plane changes can fail at speed when validation, monitoring, deployment, and rollback are not independent
summary: Candidate pattern opened in rev0010: software failures often do not require an unknown bug at the user-facing layer. They can arise when the control plane that deploys, validates, monitors, alerts, or remediates a system shares hidden assumptions with the failing path, making bad states look normal or propagate faster than governance can react.

status_history.note: Created from four software/IT engineering records and three vulnerability-infrastructure records; explicitly not an all-software-failures theory.

claims.claim: Across Knight Capital, the 2003 blackout EMS episode, Equifax, and CrowdStrike, critical software control planes showed false-normal or delayed-warning behavior at a boundary where deployment, validation, monitoring, or rollback/recovery had to be independent of the failing path.
what_would_change_status: Negative controls show these cases do not share a useful structure.
A mature synthesis splits the pattern into unrelated subpatterns.

claims.claim: CVE, NVD, and CISA KEV make publicly disclosed/exploited vulnerabilities more nameable, searchable, enriched, and prioritizable, but they are not a CSB/NTSB-equivalent for software operational failures, failed rollouts, alarm failures, monitoring blindness, or post-incident causal investigation.
what_would_change_status: An official software-incident board or comprehensive public postmortem infrastructure emerges and is recorded.
A later schema separates vulnerability rails from operational-failure rails more cleanly.

evidence_profile.source_depth: case-to-pattern synthesis over source-backed promoted records only
limitations: The pattern does not claim the four incidents are the same failure.
No prevalence estimate, probability model, or software-industry-wide causal assertion.
Needs negative controls and successful-control cases.
evidence_profile.red_team_state: rev0016 scaffold added; controls not yet promoted

type_payload.candidate_invariant: A change, vulnerability, or runtime condition crosses a software-control boundary faster or more silently than the independent validation/monitoring/rollback layer can detect and contain it.
non_equivalences: Knight is an automated-trading deployment failure, not a cyber breach.
The 2003 blackout EMS episode is a monitoring/situational-awareness failure within a larger grid event, not a vulnerability case.
Equifax is a breach and patch/monitoring failure, not a mere outage.
CrowdStrike is an update/validation outage, not a malicious exploit or Microsoft-caused incident.
Vulnerability rails are naming/prioritization infrastructure, not postmortem boards.
counterexamples_needed: successful canary/ring deployment containing a bad update
control-room alarm self-failure detected and escalated correctly
rollback worked fast enough to prevent material impact
major software incident with transparent public causal report and tracked recommendations

positive_controls_needed: Add additional software/IT failures in which control-plane or privileged changes propagated faster than independent validation/monitoring/rollback could contain.
negative_controls_needed: Add software failures caused by demand load, hardware, adversarial exploitation, or physical infrastructure rather than change propagation.
counterexamples_to_seek: A high-risk deployment where canarying, staged rollout, independent monitoring, or rollback prevented broad harm.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: High: outage, trading, grid-monitoring, breach, content-update, and vulnerability-management cases require different child mechanisms.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

handling_notes: Software failures can expose personal, medical, financial, travel, and infrastructure harms; avoid importing victim-level data or operational exploit details.
Do not turn cybersecurity records into exploit tutorials or blame spectacle.
Pattern claims must remain careful because vendor/regulator incentives and incomplete public evidence can distort postmortems.

unknowns: No denominator of software failures exists in this cube yet.
No public software-incident recommendation/action tracking surface comparable to NTSB/CSB is identified yet.
Vulnerability-infrastructure timeliness and coverage have not been audited.
next_actions: Add Therac-25 as a deeper software-safety record before pattern maturation.
Add UK Post Office Horizon as software-plus-institutional-failure record.
Add incident-postmortem infrastructure candidates such as SRE postmortem norms, software bill of materials policy, and public incident databases.
Collect negative controls and near-miss records where software controls prevented harm.
Add at least one negative-control or counterexample record before upgrading this pattern beyond candidate level.
